novelty.readme_security: NOT acknowledged. Neither README.md nor SECURITY.md acknowledges that run_end's exit_code/lingering_terminated, or the per-request vars list, are uncapped client-controlled fields reaching that same never-trimmed append path. SECURITY.md:11 lists audit-log confidentiality in scope but names no size/volume bound.
novelty.v1_v8: Same CLASS as V4 (uncapped-reason disk-fill) but a GENUINE BYPASS, which CHARTER 5 counts as novel. V4's fix caps ONLY `reason` (MAX_REASON=1000, control.py:20,163-164; regression test tests/test_control.py:263-265) and the command line (logged_command / MAX_LOGGED_COMMAND=4000, control.py:21,32-38; regression test tests/test_multiuser.py:50). I verified both caps STILL HOLD on current main (reason 1500 -> rejected). The run_end fields exit_code/lingering_terminated (control.py:277-288) and the vars list (control.py:246,263 + broker.py:113-124) are entirely uncapped and NOT covered by any V4 regression test, so the disk-fill class is reopened through fields the V4 fix missed. Not V1/V2/V3/V5/V6/V7/V8.

reasoning: ROOT CAUSE: src/envh/server/control.py:_start_run (lines 276-288) reads exit_code=note.get('exit_code') and lingering_terminated=note.get('lingering_terminated') RAW from the client's run_done note with no type or size check, then passes them to self.broker.audit.event('run_end', ..., exit_code=..., lingering_terminated=...). src/envh/core/audit.py:Audit.event (lines 42-49) serializes the full record with json.dumps(record, sort_keys=True, default=str), writes it to audit.jsonl, flush()es and os.fsync()s -- with NO per-field cap (the only truncation, _short at audit.py:84-86, applies solely to the console DISPLAY line, never to the file). The matching client-controlled fields `reason` (control.py:_reason, MAX_REASON=1000) and `command` (logged_command, MAX_LOGGED_COMMAND=4000) ARE capped -- that was the V4 fix -- but run_end's two fields, and the per-request vars=sorted(mapping) list (control.py:246,263; broker.py:113-124), are not. An AUTO key (AUTO_CANARY, policy=auto, needs_approval=false) lets a listed non-root user open an auto-approved run with NO console, reach the run_done loop, and write up to ~1 MiB of attacker-chosen bytes per run (bounded only by MAX_LINE on the run_done readline). One run per connection with no sequential rate limit makes total growth unbounded. VERDICT CONFIRMED/HIGH: (a) in scope per CHARTER 3 -- pure non-root socket client, no root/data-dir/memory read is relied on (statvfs delta is the non-root proof; grader stat of my own throwaway instance is permitted measurement only); (b) reproduced as rt1 on fresh instance e3080323e205115f with pasted output: single 900KB run accepted (no error, broker alive) and audit.jsonl +900,576 B; 10 runs -> +9,005,790 B at 900,579 B/run, ~25.6 MB/s; (c) real impact per CHARTER 4 DoS/INTEGRITY -- reliable, deterministic disk exhaustion of an append-only, never-trimmed (README:148) audit log from the socket; at ENOSPC every subsequent audit.event() fsync raises OSError, i.e. every broker action fails (full availability wedge; not pushed to ENOSPC per the task's safety constraint, but the unbounded rate is demonstrated), plus an anti-forensics effect (megabytes of noise push real events out of the console's bounded 2000-line tail and set older=True), and it degrades the shared disk for co-tenant users; (d) novel per CHARTER 5 -- a genuine bypass of the V4 cap through fields V4 and its regression tests never covered, verified by confirming the reason/command caps still hold. HIGH per CHARTER 6 ('reliable DoS'); the attacker self-assessed HIGH and I independently agree.
recommended_fix: In control.py _start_run, coerce exit_code to a bounded int (int(note.get('exit_code')) clamped, default on failure) and lingering_terminated to a bounded int/short string before logging, and cap the vars list length (as reason/command are already capped), so a client nobody approves cannot write megabytes to the never-trimmed audit log.
